title: Mahmoud Darwish and Tamar Ben Ami: The impossible love of a Palestinian poet and an Israeli dancer
subhead: In the early 1960s, in Haifa, Israel, the young Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish fell in love with Tamar Ben Ami, a Jewish Israeli dancer. Their romance was intense but brief. From this forbidden love, the writer composed a poignant poem, 'Rita and the Rifle,' which is still sung throughout the Arab world.

French court shuts down establishment hosting paid gang bangs in Paris
subhead: France's highest administrative court upheld the temporary closure of a venue that hosted these sexual activities in mid-July while awaiting a final ruling. The court found that the events at the establishment exposed women to 'serious risks' to their physical and psychological well-being, but it did not ban the practices themselves.

title: Chile: Long and twisting saga of converting President Salvador's home into a museum ends in private sale
subhead: Former Chilean president Gabriel Boric wanted to turn the site into a museum and a memorial. The home of his predecessor, who took his own life during General Pinochet's coup in 1973, was instead purchased by a private company that had outgrown its offices.

title: 'The End of Oak Street': Jurassic Park comes to suburban America
subhead: Blending prehistoric science fiction with a satire of American suburbia, David Robert Mitchell playfully subverts the conventions of Steven Spielberg's blockbuster, delivering a B-movie that is both wild and cleverly twisted.

title: Finland wants to restore its peatlands to help the environment. And to slow Russian tanks.
subhead: The Nordic country has identified 180,000 hectares of wetlands that, if restored, could benefit not only the climate and biodiversity but also national defense. While the military supports the plan, some environmentalists warn against rushing the process.
